title: harrisia fragrans subsp. aboriginum
intro: Harrisia fragrans subsp. aboriginum, commonly known as the "Night-blooming Cereus", is a species of cactus native to the southwestern regions of the United States and northern Mexico. This plant has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, sore throats, and respiratory problems, due to its numerous health benefits. Its therapeutic actions include anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antispasmodic properties, which contribute to its ability to soothe and calm the body. The bioactive constituents of Harrisia fragrans subsp. aboriginum include flavonoids, alkaloids, and glycosides, which have been identified as responsible for its medicinal properties.
